scenes.label: Brevio Studio
scenes.text: Welcome to Brevio Studio. This walkthrough follows one lecture, from choosing the source to a checked, approved video.

scenes.label: Step 1 · Source
scenes.text: Start by choosing who the video is for: researchers, the general public or kids. Here we pick kids, so the voice, tone and cards will suit children.

scenes.label: Step 1 · Advanced settings
scenes.text: Under Advanced settings you will find the options most people leave alone. Aspect ratio sets the video shape: landscape, portrait or square. Transcription quality trades speed for accuracy. The local model field names the model that picks clips on this computer. Minimum and maximum clip length limit how long each clip can be. Finally, paste the source link here. It is credited on the ending card and in the post.

scenes.label: Step 1 · Source
scenes.text: Now click Analyze source. Brevio transcribes the lecture on this computer and lists its strongest clips.

scenes.label: Step 2 · Clips
scenes.text: Each suggested clip has a Keep checkbox. Untick any clip you do not want, or tick it again to bring it back.

scenes.label: Step 2 · Clips
scenes.text: Select a clip to see it in the player. Play it, and click Set in where the clip should start. Click Set out where it should end.

scenes.label: Step 2 · Blueprint
scenes.text: Now click Generate preview. Brevio first plans a blueprint, before it writes anything. The bar shows the planned opening, clips, bridges and ending, with an estimated length inside the 30 to 60 second budget. Below it are the ideas for the opening, each bridge and the ending. Then it builds the video from that plan.

scenes.label: Step 3 · Studio
scenes.text: In the Studio, press play to watch the preview. The timeline lists the opening, each clip, the bridges and the ending.

scenes.label: Step 3 · Studio
scenes.text: Open Source evidence to see the excerpt behind the selected section. Open Blueprint to see the plan again, with a result line showing the real clip count and length.

scenes.label: Step 3 · Approval
scenes.text: A named person types their name. They confirm they reviewed the preview. Then they approve it, and nothing can be exported before that.

scenes.label: Step 4 · Export
scenes.text: Now click Export video. On the Export page, download the MP4 or the ZIP package. Open Post copy to copy the post text.

scenes.label: Step 4 · Technical check
scenes.text: The technical check covers media, captions, loudness and narration. Open any item to see what it checks and what your export shows.

scenes.label: Step 4 · Structure check
scenes.text: The structure check covers section order, bridges and narration. Five blueprint checks compare the export with the plan: clip count, clips, bridges, length and wording. Wording is compared by key words, because the video text is shortened on purpose. Each section is marked as following the plan or differing, and only a clear drift asks for review.

scenes.label: Brevio Studio
scenes.text: That is the whole workflow: choose, trim, preview, approve and export. A person reviews every video before it goes out.
